investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Because the pod never schedules, the remote agent never reaches a running/idle/ready state, and the eval runner never writes any evidence fields, producing a complete contract gap (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

Because the pod never schedules, the remote agent never reaches a running/idle/ready state, and the eval runner never writes any evidence fields, producing a complete contract gap (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). investigations.title: Remote Agent Kubernetes Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available for scheduling. Because the agent pod never started, no runtime response was produced and all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent from the eval result.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable state. The eval probe (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918: createAgent with type "remote") never receives a running agent, so it cannot collect any evidence, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler message names the exact resource constraint and node count.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=153120, pod stuck unscheduled for 146s — the probe waited the full timeout before failing, consistent with a pod that never left Pending.

sibling.remote-agent-create: same Unschedulable scheduler message, pod stuck for 121s, latencyMs=124564 — the create step failed before runtime was attempted, confirming the block is at pod scheduling, not at agent logic.
sibling.remote-agent-state: same Unschedulable scheduler message, pod stuck for 148s, latencyMs=150889 — state polling also failed, showing the scheduling block persisted across sequential eval runs.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent — consistent with the agent pod never reaching a running state where it could emit evidence.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no partial evidence was captured, confirming the probe returned before any agent API interaction occurred.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: line 1918 shows createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) is the first substantive call inside the probe — if this call blocks on pod scheduling, no downstream evidence can be collected.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false — all three failed, indicating the shared pod-scheduling dependency is the common failure point, not a contract or runner configuration issue.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the cluster's peer-pod VM slots are fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or label drift on the 4 non-kata nodes: if the pod's affinity rules are overly restrictive or node labels changed, the 4 non-kata nodes would be permanently excluded regardless of available general capacity. The scheduler message '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' is consistent with this but does not distinguish a pre-existing correct constraint from a regression.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, and their combined VM slot quota may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs plus any live workloads. No node-count or quota configuration evidence is present in the packet to confirm or rule this out.

UNLIKELY — eval runner misconfiguration causing incorrect pod spec: if the pod spec submitted by createAgent incorrectly requests kata.peerpods.io/vm or sets wrong affinity labels, the scheduling failure would be self-inflicted. This is less likely because the same runner has presumably passed previously (though no passing history is recorded in verifierContext.history).

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 kata-capable nodes shows available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots remaining, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and the affinity/selector mismatch or a pod spec error would need to be investigated instead.

If a remote-agent pod successfully schedules and reaches Running state during the same time window on a different cluster or namespace, the failure is environment-specific rather than a global capacity issue.

If the eval runner passes immediately after a re-run with no cluster changes, the failure may have been transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent workloads temporarily consuming all VM slots) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If no other pods are consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, the quota ceiling itself may be set too low in the node configuration rather than being consumed by live workloads.
